findings.action: Define the exact fail-closed policy matrix for 'augments missing (미제공)' across average placement, Top4/1st ratio metrics, relative metrics, and CSV export in planning-draft.md, and reconcile the contradiction between source-research.md (CompositionFingerprintBuilder includes augments; MetricPolicy.AugmentRestriction only passes empty augment lists) and planning-draft.md's claim that composition/item ratio statistics can be served while only augment filters/metrics are blocked.
findings.impact: If MetricPolicy.AugmentRestriction currently blocks ratio/relative metrics whenever augments are non-empty or unclassified, either (a) a strict fail-closed treatment of 'missing augments' will block all ratio/relative metrics for real matches too (leaving the user with no ratio statistics even after Phase 2), or (b) allowing composition/item ratio metrics when augments are missing will silently bypass the very AugmentRestriction policy that prevented mapping missing augments to an empty list.

findings.action: Add a quantitative sample-size and collection-volume analysis to planning-draft.md showing how many real matches must be collected to reach n >= 100 per composition (exact unit list + active synergies, plus item condition filters), what metrics remain visible when n < 100 (e.g., count/average placement vs. hidden ratio metrics), and whether coarser aggregation or collection-scale adjustments are needed in Phase 2.
findings.impact: planning-draft.md recognizes that 128 incomplete records (1,024 participant rows) cannot reach n >= 100 per composition, but assumes Option B or raising the storage cap in Option C solves the issue. Because exact (unit list + active synergies) fingerprints have high cardinality in TFT, reaching n >= 100 for a single composition (and even more so with item filters) requires hundreds to thousands of matches per patch/set—meaning real data may still produce zero visible ratio metrics under single-user API collection limits.

findings.action: Make Option B's entry gate in planning-draft.md explicitly contingent on authoritative/official verification of new data_version semantics and deterministic patch-to-catalog provenance (not just empirical shape inspection of <= 20 matches in Phase 1), or else route unverified schemas strictly to Option C (isolated reference statistics) or Option D (hold).
findings.impact: planning-draft.md implies that Phase 1 shape diagnosis of up to 20 matches is sufficient to select Option B (merging real matches into confirmed patch statistics). However, source-research.md and storage-support-options.md explicitly forbid accepting undocumented data_version values or promoting unverified releases into confirmed catalog/patch analytics without official or equivalent authoritative semantic proof.

findings.action: Constrain Phase 1 extraction of '앞의 두 숫자 그룹 값(릴리스 후보)' from game_version to strict bounds (e.g., only extract 1-2 digit numbers when preceded by a known release prefix/delimiter pattern, and otherwise record only the masked shape signature '9'/'a' and digit-group lengths), and specify where the Phase 1 report is stored and its retention/cleanup rules.
findings.impact: Because the diagnosed game_version strings already failed the standard numeric release pattern, the first two numeric groups in an arbitrary non-matching string could be build IDs, timestamps, or other long numeric tokens rather than release numbers. Extracting raw numeric group values without digit-length bounds (unlike data_version, which is bounded to 1-3 digits) risks recording raw unverified payload tokens in violation of the strict de-identification boundary.
